RUBRIC.title: Monthly aggregation
RUBRIC.method: Sum revenue by product and year-month.

RUBRIC.title: Selling price
RUBRIC.method: Divide monthly revenue by the same month’s units sold.

RUBRIC.title: Clearance identification
RUBRIC.method: Identify the recurring lower-price month for each product.

RUBRIC.title: Returns matched to sales
RUBRIC.method: Divide returns booked in t+1 by originating units in t.

RUBRIC.title: Warranties matched to sales
RUBRIC.method: Divide warranty claims booked in t+2 by originating units in t.

TAXONOMY.title: Incomplete answer
TAXONOMY.description: An assessed answer cell is blank.
TAXONOMY.hint: Complete the highlighted answer cell using a calculation from your analysis.

TAXONOMY.title: Spreadsheet calculation error
TAXONOMY.description: The saved answer contains an Excel error.
TAXONOMY.hint: Trace the formula precedents and resolve the error in Excel before saving again.

TAXONOMY.title: Formula result unavailable
TAXONOMY.description: A formula is present, but the file has no saved result. This is not evidence of an accounting mistake.
TAXONOMY.hint: Recalculate and save the workbook in desktop Excel, then select the saved file again.

TAXONOMY.title: Units used for revenue
TAXONOMY.description: The answer matches monthly units instead of monthly dollar sales.
TAXONOMY.hint: Check the units of the requested output. Aggregate the revenue column for the specified product and year-month.

TAXONOMY.title: Same month pooled across years
TAXONOMY.description: The answer matches all occurrences of that calendar month across the ten-year dataset.
TAXONOMY.hint: Use both year and month in the filter. February 2012 is one period, not every February.

TAXONOMY.title: Average used for total
TAXONOMY.description: The answer matches average daily revenue rather than monthly total revenue.
TAXONOMY.hint: Check whether the question requests an average or a total and review the aggregation operation.

TAXONOMY.title: Product columns mixed
TAXONOMY.description: The answer matches the other product for the requested month.
TAXONOMY.hint: Trace the product label through the sales, claims, and answer columns.

TAXONOMY.title: Adjacent period selected
TAXONOMY.description: The answer matches a neighboring sales month.
TAXONOMY.hint: Check date boundaries, including the year and the first day of the next month.

TAXONOMY.title: Price ratio inverted
TAXONOMY.description: The answer matches units divided by revenue.
TAXONOMY.hint: Write down the units: dollars divided by units produces dollars per unit.

TAXONOMY.title: Claim booking month mistaken for sales cohort
TAXONOMY.description: The answer matches claims booked in the sales month divided by that month’s units.
TAXONOMY.hint: Returns from sales in t are booked in t+1; warranties from sales in t are booked in t+2. Trace one cohort.

TAXONOMY.title: Answer describes the prior cohort
TAXONOMY.description: The answer matches claims booked in t divided by sales in t minus the policy lag.
TAXONOMY.hint: That can describe an earlier cohort correctly, but the answer cell asks about sales originating in the specified month.

TAXONOMY.title: One-month lag used for warranty
TAXONOMY.description: The answer matches next-month warranty claims divided by current sales.
TAXONOMY.hint: Warranty claims in this case are booked two months after the originating sale.

TAXONOMY.title: Dollar sales used in a unit claim rate
TAXONOMY.description: The answer matches the correct claim count divided by revenue.
TAXONOMY.hint: The numerator counts products. Use originating units sold so numerator and denominator have compatible units.

TAXONOMY.title: Returns deducted from the denominator
TAXONOMY.description: The answer matches claims divided by units remaining after returns.
TAXONOMY.hint: The case’s technical answer uses original units sold, rather than units net of later returns.

TAXONOMY.title: Claim count reported as a rate
TAXONOMY.description: The answer matches a claim count rather than its proportion of originating sales.
TAXONOMY.hint: Divide the matched claim count by units sold in the originating sales month.

TAXONOMY.title: Percentage scale mismatch
TAXONOMY.description: The answer is consistent with a factor-of-100 conversion error.
TAXONOMY.hint: 8.38% and 0.0838 are equivalent. The number 8.38 without a percent sign represents 838%.

TAXONOMY.title: Clearance month representation
TAXONOMY.description: The answer uses a number or abbreviated month instead of the requested full month name.
TAXONOMY.hint: Use the complete English month name, such as September, as specified in the case.

TAXONOMY.title: Clearance period identification
TAXONOMY.description: The submitted month does not match the recurring lower-price month in this dataset.
TAXONOMY.hint: Calculate monthly revenue divided by monthly units. Look for the recurring reduction in selling price.

TAXONOMY.title: Method needs investigation
TAXONOMY.description: The answer differs, but it does not uniquely match a supported mistake pattern.
TAXONOMY.hint: Trace the calculation from source data. An incorrect number alone does not identify the method used.
